rationale: All four blocking findings from code-review.final are resolved. CR-001 (INTERRUPTED states skipped at startup): startup_recovery.py inner predicate now checks both IN_PROGRESS and INTERRUPTED, confirmed by direct file read. CR-002 (single exception aborts scan): per-level exception handling at status-bucket, execution, and state levels verified in current startup_recovery.py. CR-003 (plain 'execution_id' vs EXECUTION_ID_KEYWORD): import and usage of the constant confirmed in startup_recovery.py line 21 and 50. CR-004 (missing double-failure test): check diff explicitly adds test_original_exception_raised_when_both_state_writes_fail, mocking both finish_state and get_by_id to raise, asserting original RuntimeError still propagates. Confidence medium rather than high because the fix-up diff does not include startup_recovery.py or test_startup_recovery.py as explicit hunks; CR-001/002/003 resolution was confirmed by direct file read rather than check diff evidence. No new high-risk issues introduced by the fix-up diff. The fail() cleanup block uses a single outer try/except, which is a less-than-ideal pattern, but this is an active-execution error path (not a startup scan) consistent with the pre-existing abort() implementation and does not introduce data loss risk.

finding_status.notes: startup_recovery.py inner predicate at line 59-62 now reads `state.status in (WorkflowExecutionStatusEnum.IN_PROGRESS, WorkflowExecutionStatusEnum.INTERRUPTED)`, matching the pattern used in fail(). Both orphan types recovered at startup. Confirmed by direct file read (not visible as a discrete hunk in the check diff).

startup_recovery.py now has three independent exception scopes: per-terminal-status bucket (lines 39-46, continues to next status on DB query failure), per-execution (lines 48-57, skips that execution on state query failure), and per-state (lines 63-72, logs and continues to next state on save failure). A single corrupt row no longer aborts the entire scan. test_save_error_does_not_abort_scan directly verifies that good_state.save() is still called when bad_state.save() raises.

startup_recovery.py imports EXECUTION_ID_KEYWORD from workflow_execution_service (line 21) and uses it in the WorkflowExecutionState query (line 50: `fields={EXECUTION_ID_KEYWORD: execution.execution_id}`). ES term-match vs full-text divergence eliminated.

test_original_exception_raised_when_both_state_writes_fail added to test_base_node_lifecycle.py. Test mocks finish_state to raise OSError and WorkflowExecutionState.get_by_id to also raise OSError, then asserts that the original RuntimeError('node execute failed') is still re-raised unconditionally. The double-failure code path in base_node.py lines 272-287 is now covered.
